doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Jazz parties as a social oasis
summary: Jazz parties mean little playing but reunions with old friends like Kenny Davern and meeting Joe Cohn.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah. I’ll have to remember that if I’m down there. What’s on the bill for you coming up? Obviously you’re down here playing these festivals. Do you like doing these jazz parties?

The fun of it for me — you know there’s not much playing to do. It’s mostly waiting around to play. And so from that point of view they are kind of frustrating. You leave four days or three days later not having hardly played more than forty minutes. There’s ten piano players here, and only one of us can appear at a time so I played twenty minutes today, wait all day and play twenty minutes tomorrow night, wait another day and play forty minutes. That’s the downside. The upside is I get to see people that I haven’t seen in years and you can see how I love to talk, this — I love to be able to tell stories and talk and get into stuff, and that’s what happens here. Because people like Kenny Davern for instance, who I’ve known for forty years, we talk about the same things all the time, but we still like to do it. So I see a lot of old people — old people is right — old cronies. And then I meet younger people that I’d never get a chance to meet, like I met Al Cohn’s son here, Joe Cohn, he was about the best guitar player I ever heard in my life, and meeting him was a pleasure. I never would have met him. Because the work I do now is all by myself. I just do a solo act. So this is a social oasis for me you know, and I like it for that.
It is great fun to just like hang out in the lobby and watch.
It’s a little like a class reunion, it really is.
